McLaren: McLaren has reshaped the front‑suspension fairings and trimmed the front‑wing flap to tighten the car’s aerodynamic balance, giving the driver a more predictable front end through the high‑speed corners. At the rear, both the main wing and the beam wing have been dialed down – the wing’s profile is slimmer and set to a low‑downforce mode – which cuts drag and lets the car carry more speed on the straights. Together these tweaks should make the car feel steadier in the bends while maximizing straight‑line pace for this weekend’s circuit.
Scuderia Ferrari: Ferrari has trimmed the front‑wing flap to a shorter “chord” shape, giving the car a tighter balance that helps it turn more predictably through the corner‑heavy sections of the track. At the back, they’ve lightened the top‑side rear‑wing elements and added a more flexible flap, while the lower beam wing now runs as a single, slimmer piece – both moves cut drag and boost straight‑line speed. In short, the new aero package should keep the car stable in the bends while letting it carry more speed onto the straights, a key advantage for this weekend’s layout.
Red Bull Racing: Red Bull has trimmed the front‑wing flaps and reshaped the floor, giving the car a cleaner airflow and a bit more grip on the straights and in fast corners. The new fence shapes and a re‑profiled floor edge act like a subtle “skate‑blade,” tightening the car’s balance and making it easier to get on the power early in the weekend. In short, the aero tweaks should translate into more consistent cornering speed and better tyre wear, giving them a solid edge right out of the gate.
Mercedes F1 Team: Mercedes has tweaked three key aero pieces for the weekend: a tiny reshaping of the rear‑wing tip to shave off a bit of drag, a re‑angled out‑board floor fence that smooths the airflow under the car, and a slightly flatter front‑wing flap to give the front end a more predictable bite. Together these changes should boost straight‑line speed while keeping the car stable through fast corners, giving the drivers a tighter, more confident feel on the track.
Aston Martin: Aston Martin has added a new, less‑aggressive flap to the rear wing, giving the car a wider drag range that can be dialed in for this circuit’s mix of straights and corners. The tweak lets the team fine‑tune straight‑line speed without losing too much down‑force in the slower sections, meaning the car should be quicker off the line and more stable through the bends this weekend.

Haas F1 Team: Haas has fitted a circuit‑specific front wing that tweaks the aerodynamic balance across the car. By fine‑tuning the wing’s “balance range,” the team expects more stable front‑end grip and smoother tyre wear, which should translate into better cornering and overall pace this weekend. In short, the new wing is designed to give Haas a more predictable, faster car on the track.
Racing Bulls / RB: Racing Bulls has tweaked several aero pieces for this weekend’s track, giving the car a cleaner, more efficient shape. The new rear‑wing and mirror housings cut drag, while the revised under‑floor and side‑pod panels improve down‑force without adding extra resistance. In short, the car should be quicker on the straights and stick to the corners better, giving the drivers a real performance edge.
Williams Racing: Williams is trialling a new trim on both the front and rear wing flaps that subtly reshapes the trailing edges. The tweak reduces drag, giving the car a bit more straight‑line speed without sacrificing too much downforce. If it works, the extra top‑end pace could make a real difference in qualifying and the race this weekend.
